A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OminiControl. All 15 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v4, including their five-page appendices, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, ablations, dataset statistics, and a user study with 375 valid responses in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including quantitative benchmark comparisons, ablations, and the appendix user study.

M1.justification: Both versions use VAE-encoded condition tokens, joint multimodal attention, task-dependent position offsets, LoRA adaptation, and an inference-time conditioning bias. Reorganization and expanded explanations do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain five spatially aligned tasks evaluated on COCO, DreamBooth subject-driven evaluation, Subjects200K, and the appendix scene-variation and try-on examples. v4 newly identifies the spatial training source; it does not establish newly added data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain SD1.5 ControlNet and T2I-Adapter, FLUX ControlNetPro, IP-Adapter on SD1.5 and FLUX, and SSR-Encoder. SSR-Encoder already appears in v1's figures and Table S1; added related-work citations are not new evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The main-text synthesis description revises the reported count from over 20,000 descriptions to over 30,000. Appendix A's detailed generation counts remain unchanged, so this does not establish regeneration. Evaluation splits, resolutions, model variants, optimizer settings, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The attention, position-shift, training-data, conditioning-strength, LoRA-rank, and conditioning-depth analyses retain their evidence. Appendix failure examples also remain unchanged. Calling Figure 10's spatial condition depth rather than Canny corrects the description of an existing illustration.

E5.justification: Both specify seed 42 for spatial evaluation and five seeds for subject-driven evaluation, reporting averages and best scores over those seeds. Figure 4's shaded bands remain unchanged, and no new uncertainty estimates or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces every CLIP-Score, including Ours/Canny from 0.76 to 0.308. The depth winner changes to SD1.5 T2I-Adapter, and the Mask ranking reverses. Other experimental numbers and visual results remain unchanged. Section 4.2 also incorrectly reassigns Canny's F1 of 0.38 to depth. These are reporting revisions, not established performance changes.

T1.justification: v4's biased-attention expression uses [CT; X; CI], matching the bias matrix's M, N, N block dimensions and correcting v1's mismatch with Z = [X; CT; CI]. The new position-offset equation otherwise restates the existing strategy; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: parameter reuse with approximately 0.1% additional parameters, unified spatially aligned and non-aligned control, superior baseline performance, and the Subjects200K dataset and synthesis pipeline.

C2.justification: v4 newly describes the bias as scaling cross-token attention weights by log(gamma). This mechanism explanation is misleading: the displayed equation adds log(gamma) to logits, producing a gamma factor before normalization. Interpretations concerning overfitting, conditioning depth, and appendix failure cases otherwise remain stable.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies the last 300,000 images of text-to-image-2M as spatial training data. Conversely, v1's explicit shifted position ranges are replaced by an unspecified fixed offset in v4. Hardware, other hyperparameters, appendix synthesis instructions, and resource destinations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References add rectified-flow-transformer work, multimodal speech-emotion attention, InstantBooth, ELITE, and FastComposer, while removing ControlNet++, ControlNeXt, ControlNet-XS, and Visual Autoregressive Modeling. The principal positioning against ControlNet and IP-Adapter and the unified-control novelty claim remain stable.

P1.justification: The introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten. v1 Sections 3.2–3.4 become named paragraphs within v4 Section 3.2, and dataset synthesis receives a staged narrative. Contributions are reordered, broken sentences are repaired, and an acknowledgment is added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is resized, Table 3 moves from page 8 to page 9, and Figure 6's caption is shortened alongside main-text reflow. No figures, tables, or plotted series are added or removed. Appendix displays remain unchanged apart from citation numbers.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition and disclosure of the spatial training source improve documentation. However, unexplained CLIP-Score replacements introduce a discrepancy between Table 1's Canny score of 0.308 and Table 3's retained default score of 0.761, while Section 4.2 introduces a depth/F1 mislabel. The PDFs do not resolve these reporting problems, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
